newsitem.title: INDIA: At least 18 killed by militants in northeast India.
newsitem.headline: At least 18 killed by militants in northeast India.

text.p: At least 18 people were killed in an ambush by tribal militants in India's remote northeastern state of Tripura early on Tuesday, police said.
Police in Agartala, state capital of Tripura, told Reuters by telephone that they suspected the National Liberation Front of Tripura, a separatist guerrilla group, was responsible for the attack.
The incident took place at Chamanu in Dhalai district, some 180 km (120 miles) north of Agartala.
The victims were travelling in two vehicles when the militants opened fire from a hill-top, killing most of them on the spot, the police said.
Police said 15 of the deceased belonged to the paramilitary General Reserve Engineering Force while three were casual labourers. They said several people were wounded in the ambush.
"This is a very serious incident and all senior officials have left for the spot, we can give you more details when they come back," the official said.
Dozens of guerrilla groups in northeastern India have been fighting for independent homelands.
